problem: Mapping how work really gets done takes consultants months; Ontora agents interview employees to discover processes and prioritize AI opportunities.
business_model: AI transformation service and platform sold to enterprises

founders.name: Leon Iwanowitsch
founders.background_notes: YC page says AI consulting for enterprise and building a large European startup conference.

competitors.name: Skan AI
competitors.what: Captures how people work to map processes

technical_complexity.rationale: Conversational agents plus a company context layer with API, MCP and CLI connections; standard LLM engineering with data integration.

defensibility.rationale: The accumulated company context layer may create stickiness, but interviewing with LLMs is easy to copy.

market_need_then: Founders say company knowledge is mostly unwritten; one customer example, Pilot Group, scoped six AI initiatives from over 200 employee conversations in two weeks (company site).

identity.logo: Site links a brand page with logos

brand_strength.rationale: Name is distinctive and has the exact .com, with a podcast interview as the only brand press; no sourced recognition.

outcome_analysis: Ontora is a Spring 2026 YC company with no outcome yet. The founders bring consulting, Porsche and prior exit experience, which fits an enterprise sales motion, while process mining incumbents and consultancies are strong alternatives.
notes: Aggregators report $500K pre-seed (FundedIQ, VCBacked) but no primary confirmation; unverified. The site lists many backers including Combination VC and Webflow without amounts or dates, so no round recorded. Aggregators place the company in Dover, US while YC lists Berlin. YC page bios differ slightly from the founder story section. Audit fix: the $500K pre-seed (2026-06) is now recorded from FundedIQ; VCBacked also reports $500K with Y Combinator but no date. It rests on databases only.
